title: WIOCC Second-Floor Office Network, Security and Safety Systems
summary: Ideal Solutions delivered LAN, Wi-Fi, CCTV, access control and safety systems for WIOCC Nigeria Limited's second-floor office setup.
challenge:
WIOCC Nigeria Limited’s second-floor office setup brought together requirements for connectivity, surveillance, controlled entry and building safety. The scope extended from the network used by office equipment to the systems supporting access, fire detection and electrical protection. Each of these areas formed part of the same office infrastructure project.

The requirement therefore involved several distinct technical disciplines. Wired LAN and Wi-Fi infrastructure addressed connectivity, while CCTV and door access control addressed surveillance and entry. The brief also included an addressable fire alarm system, earthing and grounding, and lightning protection, giving the project a broader remit than an office networking installation alone.
result:
The delivered project covered the principal technology and safety systems specified for WIOCC’s second-floor office setup. Its scope joined wired and wireless connectivity with CCTV, access control and fire detection, alongside the supporting earthing, grounding and lightning protection work.

For WIOCC, the project represented a combined office infrastructure delivery spanning communications, electronic security and protection systems. It illustrates Ideal Solutions’ work across the different technical requirements that sit within a modern office fit-out.

seo.metaTitle: WIOCC Office Network & Security Case Study | Ideal Solutions
seo.metaDescription: Explore Ideal Solutions' delivery of LAN, Wi-Fi, CCTV, access control, fire alarm and protection systems for WIOCC's second-floor office setup.

solutionNarrative: Ideal Solutions delivered the office connectivity scope through network LAN and Wi-Fi infrastructure. These elements covered the wired and wireless sides of the office setup and formed the communications component of the wider project.

Alongside this work, the team delivered surveillance and CCTV systems and door access control. This brought the office’s electronic security requirements into the project scope, covering both observation of the environment and control of entry points.

The safety and protection work included an addressable fire alarm system, earthing and grounding, and a lightning and thunder arrestor system. Together, these work areas brought network, security and building-support infrastructure into one delivery scope.

title: Paxton Access Control Installation for Open Access Data Centres
summary: Ideal Solutions installed an access control system for OADC, including Paxton Net2 controllers, readers, electromagnetic locks and supporting cabling.
challenge:
Open Access Data Centres required an access-control installation covering the equipment at controlled doors and the infrastructure supporting it. The brief included controllers, readers and electromagnetic locks, together with power supplies, backup batteries and the cabling needed to connect those components.

Door access also involved exit and emergency-release equipment. Exit buttons, break-glass units and override switches were part of the specified scope, alongside associated civil works. The requirement therefore covered the full physical installation around the access points, from user-facing hardware to power and supporting works.
solution: Power supply units with backup batteries.
result:
OADC’s installation brought together Paxton access-control hardware, readers and electromagnetic locks with supporting power, batteries and cabling. The delivered scope also incorporated exit and emergency-release components and the associated civil works.

The project demonstrates an access-control delivery that encompasses the equipment visible at the door and the supporting infrastructure behind it. For this data-centre environment, Ideal Solutions’ recorded work covered the control hardware, power provision, connection infrastructure and release components within a single installation scope.

The team’s work extended to exit buttons, emergency break-glass units and emergency override switches. Associated civil works completed the specified installation scope, addressing the physical infrastructure surrounding the door-control equipment.

title: 3DCIM Environmental Monitoring Hardware Supply for OADC
summary: Ideal Solutions supplied environmental monitoring and network hardware for deployment across five OADC data halls, including 307 wireless temperature and humidity sensors.
challenge:
OADC’s 3DCIM project required environmental monitoring and network hardware for deployment across five data halls. The specified equipment included 307 wireless temperature and humidity sensors, making sensor supply a substantial part of the requirement.

The wider brief also covered cooling duty meters, wireless receivers, rack equipment and PoE switches. Supplying the sensors was one part of a broader hardware requirement that brought together environmental measurement, wireless data reception and the network and rack equipment supporting the deployment.
result:
The completed supply provided environmental monitoring and network hardware for a deployment spanning five OADC data halls. The documented quantities include 307 wireless temperature and humidity sensors, supported by cooling duty meters, wireless receivers, rack equipment and PoE switches.

The project illustrates Ideal Solutions’ role in supplying specialised data-centre hardware across several related equipment categories. Its recorded output is the provision of the hardware package for the five-hall scope, with both environmental sensing and supporting infrastructure represented in the supply.

title: Data Centre Equipment Decommissioning and Relocation from Medallion to OADC

The work involved handling installed equipment as well as moving it between facilities. Each part of the physical scope needed to account for the equipment and cabling involved, from deinstallation at the originating site through preparation for transit and handling at the destination.
solution: Equipment and cable identification and labelling.
Deinstallation and decommissioning of data-centre equipment.
Equipment packaging and preparation for transportation.
result:
The delivered work covered the physical relocation of data-centre equipment from Medallion to OADC. Equipment identification, cabling labels, decommissioning, packaging, loading, transportation and offloading were all represented within the documented scope.

For OADC, this brought the practical stages of the equipment move into a coordinated relocation service. The project demonstrates Ideal Solutions’ experience in the physical handling and logistics of data-centre infrastructure, including the preparation and transport activities surrounding a facility move.

title: Network and Wireless Infrastructure for South West Bitumen's Ore Facility

The brief also extended to wireless access points, outdoor wireless equipment and network configuration. Delivering the scope involved both the physical network installation and configuration work, with indoor and outdoor wireless elements included in the facility’s connectivity requirements.
result:
The delivered scope at SWB’s Ore facility combined network equipment, Cat6 cabling, racks, PDUs and UPS equipment with wireless access points and outdoor wireless infrastructure. Both installation and configuration were included in the work described for the project.

The result was a network infrastructure delivery spanning the wired, wireless, equipment-mounting and power-support elements of the brief. The project shows how Ideal Solutions brings these related work areas together within an industrial facility’s connectivity deployment.
